errors.title: An early terminal observation becomes irrevocable before the assignment has released
errors.reproducer: Run the r2 sandbox probes.py. For terminal-then-active/idle/interrupted/missing, events first admit w-1 and assign /root/writer, then record completed/reconciled, then a later nonterminal/unknown observation BEFORE the result, and only afterward record the passed/reconciled result. Each probe snapshots, resumes with the matching live lifecycle, and appends admission of w-2. Captured exact commands and outputs are in results.json; each directory retains admission.json and its log.
errors.expected: Before both release facts are established, a newer active or unknown lifecycle must invalidate reliance on an earlier terminal observation, or the contradictory event must be explicitly rejected as requiring reconciliation. Resume and append must keep the writer barrier until a fresh terminal reconciliation. Retain historical fully released assignments without inventing a new barrier merely because a completed worker disappears later.
errors.actual: All four histories validate, their snapshots visibly show the newer active/idle/interrupted/missing unknown state, resume returns admission_allowed=true, and append accepts the second writer. validate and execution_facts ignore every later observation once any completed/reconciled observation appears, even when the task result had not yet arrived. command_resume also derives advice only from those retained old facts. The fresh-terminal control succeeds as it should; properly reassigned same-handle work correctly blocks old-completion reuse.
errors.fix_verification: Add the four preserved orderings and a fresh terminal control. Make release a fact of a fully reconciled assignment, not a permanently absorbing first terminal observation. Current live active/unknown contradictions must not be hidden by a historical terminal fact; separate historical release from latest handle state explicitly. Preserve result-first/observation-first success, historical missing released handles, same-handle fresh assignment barriers and append-only unknown reconciliation.

errors.title: Invalid UTF-8 bypasses structured rejection and prevents repairing a derived snapshot
errors.reproducer: The r2 probes create utf8/invalid.json containing one 0xff byte, then pass it to append --event, resume --agents and init --criteria. They also replace snapshot.json with that byte while preserving a valid events.jsonl, then invoke resume with a valid empty agents array. Exact commands and stderr are in results.json.
errors.expected: Invalid UTF-8 supplied as JSON data returns exit 2 with one JSON data error. Invalid UTF-8 in a derived snapshot must be treated as corrupt/stale and regenerated from the valid authoritative log. Log bytes must remain unchanged. The existing invalid-authoritative-log control must continue to preserve derived bytes.
errors.actual: All four commands exit 1 with uncaught UnicodeDecodeError tracebacks. read_events handles UnicodeDecodeError, but read_json does not; bound_snapshot does not catch it either. Thus corruption confined to a disposable projection blocks the documented valid-log recovery path.
errors.fix_verification: Exercise invalid UTF-8 for criteria, single-event append, live-agent input, authoritative JSONL and derived snapshot. Require structured rejection for input/log cases, successful projection repair for a valid log plus bad snapshot, and unchanged authoritative bytes throughout. Preserve existing wrong-type, duplicate-key and nonfinite controls.
